title: Greedy partner choice bound
statement: Let $r,k,s$ be natural numbers with $r>0$ and $s>0$, and let $R$ be a finite set of vertices in $2r$ parts of size $k$ with $|R|=2s$. Choose a part containing the largest number of vertices of $R$, and choose a pivot vertex from that part. The number of vertices of $R$ in parts other than the pivot's part is at most $\frac{2r-1}{r}s$.
hypotheses_covered: $R$ is a finite set of vertices in $2r$ parts of size $k$
